Rashi on Shabbat 39b:1:1.hebrew: בטלה הטמנה - נאסרה הטמנה בדבר המוסיף הבל, דהא מבע"י נתנו שם הסילון, ומפני שהצוננין מתחממין בכך, ואע"ג דממילא — אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 39b:1:1.english: Insulating was abolished - Insulating in something that increases heat was prohibited, for they placed the pipe there while it was still day; and because the cold [water] is heated through this, even though [it occurs] on its own, it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:1:2.english: Their pipes - [Meaning,] their pipes, for they retracted [their position].

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:3:1.hebrew: ראויין לשתיה - דמחים להו לשתייה, ואי בעי רוחץ בהן פניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 39b:3:1.english: Fit for drinking - That he heats them for drinking, and if he wishes, he washes his face with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:4:1.english: To rinse - That he pours [water] over his body and rinses off.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:4:2.hebrew: והאי תנא - ר' שמעון היא, דמתיר להשתטף כל גופו בשבת בחמין שהוחמו מע"ש. והיינו דקאמר: כחמין שהוחמו בשבת — אסור, הא שהוחמו מאתמול — שרי. ואי בי"ט — כחמין שהוחמו בי"ט, ואסור ברחיצה, דאפי' בית הלל לא שרי להחם בי"ט אלא לפניו, ידיו ורגליו, אבל לשיטוף כל גופו — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 39b:4:2.english: And this Tanna - [Our Mishnah] is [according to] Rabbi Shimon, who permits rinsing one’s entire body on Shabbat with hot water that was heated on the eve of Shabbat. And that is why it stated: Like hot water that was heated on Shabbat, [it is] forbidden — which implies that [water] that was heated yesterday is permitted. And regarding Yom Tov — [it is] like hot water that was heated on Yom Tov, and is forbidden for bathing, for even Beit Hillel only permitted heating [water] on Yom Tov for one’s face, hands, and feet, but for rinsing one’s entire body, [they did] not.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:4:3.english: One may not rinse - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:4:4.english: Whether with hot water - And even if it was heated on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:1.hebrew: בכלי - דהרואה אומר: "היום הוחמו", ומוכחא מילתא דתולדות האור נינהו, ואתי להחם בשבת, כגון נותן צונן בחמין:
Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:1.english: In a vessel - For an onlooker says: “[The water] was heated today,” and it is evident that it is a derivative of fire, and he will come to heat [water] on Shabbat, such as placing cold [water] into hot [water].

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:2.hebrew: אבל בקרקע - כגון אמבטאות של מרחצאות, והן חמי האור:
Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:2.english: However, in the ground - Such as the bathtubs of bathhouses, and they are [filled with water] heated by fire:

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:3.english: [It is] permitted - For they have lost the status of hot water.

Rashi on Shabbat 39b:5:4.english: Wasn’t the incident involving the people of Tiberias, etc. - Evidently, [the waters] retain their status [as hot water].

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:1:1.hebrew: ממעשה שעשו אנשי טבריא ואסרו להם בטלה הטמנה מבע"י בדבר המוסיף הבל - וא"ת: מה צריך למילף ממעשה דאנשי טבריא? הא מתני' היא דאין טומנין בדבר המוסיף הבל בפרק במה טומנין (לקמן שבת ד' מז: ושם), ומבע"י איירי, דמשחשיכה אפי' בדבר שאינו מוסיף הבל אסור, כדאמרינן בפ"ב (לעיל שבת דף לד.)! ואור"י: דמתניתין דלקמן איכא לאוקמא בבין השמשות, אבל מבעוד יום ה"א דשרי. וא"ת: והא קתני: "טומנין בגיזי צמר ואין מטלטלין אותן", ואי בין השמשות — איך טומנין בהן? והא אסור לטלטלן! וי"ל: דהוה מוקמינן כר', דאמר (לעיל שבת ד' ח:): "כל דבר שהוא משום שבות לא גזרו עליו בין השמשות". וא"ת: אי כר' אתיא — אי מבעוד יום שרי להטמין, ביה"ש נמי שרי, ד"כל דבר שהוא משום שבות כו'"! וי"ל: דה"א בהטמנה החמירו. וה"ר שמואל מוורדין מפרש: ממעשה אנשי טבריא בטלה הטמנה — דאסור אפי' לאכול, כדקתני: "ואסורין בשתיה". וה"ר יונה מפרש: בטלה — אפי' בקדירה חייתא; והיינו דקאמר "בטלה", משמע לגמרי מכל דבר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:1:1.english: "From the incident that the people of Tiberias performed and [the Sages] prohibited them, insulation while it is still day in something that adds heat was abolished" - And if you say: Why is it necessary to derive [this] from the incident of the people of Tiberias? Isn't it a Mishnah that one may not insulate in something that adds heat, in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Tomnin (below, Shabbat 47b and there)? And it is dealing with [insulating] while it is still day (mibe'od yom), because once it has grown dark, even in something that does not add heat it is forbidden, as we say in the second chapter (above, Shabbat 34a)! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that the Mishnah below can be established as referring to twilight (bein hashemashot), but while it is still day I would have said that it is permitted. And if you say: But doesn't it teach: "One may insulate with shearings of wool, but one may not handle them"? And if [it is referring to] twilight, how may one insulate with them? Behold, it is forbidden to handle them! And one can say that we would have established [the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who said (above, Shabbat 8b): Anything that is [prohibited] on account of a rabbinic decree (shevut), they did not decree against it at twilight. And if you say: If it follows Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], if while it is still day it is permitted to insulate, at twilight it should also be permitted, for "anything that is [prohibited] on account of a rabbinic decree, etc."! And one can say that I would have said that with regard to insulation they were [more] stringent. And the Rabbi, Rabbi Samuel of Verdun, explains: From the incident of the people of Tiberias insulation was abolished [in the sense] that it is forbidden even to eat [the food], as it teaches: "and they are forbidden for drinking." And the Rabbi, Rabbi Jonah, explains: It was abolished even with regard to a pot of raw [food] (kedeira ḥayyata). And that is why it says "was abolished," which implies completely, in all circumstances.

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:2:1.hebrew: הא חמין שהוחמו מבעוד יום מותרים והתניא חמין שהוחמו כו' - תימה: לוקי ההיא ברייתא דאסרה — בכלי, משום דהרואה אומר "היום הוחמו", ומתניתין — בקרקע כמשמעה, כדמפליג בסמוך בין כלי לקרקע? וי"ל דדוקא בשיטוף דקיל איכא לפלוגי, אבל ברחיצה דחמירא — לא מסתברא לפלוגי בהכי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:2:1.english: "However, hot water that was heated while it was still day is permitted? But wasn't it taught: Hot water that was heated..." - [This is] astonishing: Let [the Gemara] establish that baraita, which prohibited [bathing], as [referring to water] in a vessel, because an onlooker says, "It was heated today," and our Mishnah as [referring to water] in the ground according to its plain meaning, as [the Gemara] differentiates shortly between a vessel and the ground? And one can say that specifically regarding rinsing, which is lenient, one can differentiate [between a vessel and the ground]; but regarding bathing, which is stringent, it is not reasonable to differentiate in this manner.

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:2:2.hebrew: אלא פניו ידיו ורגליו כו' - הכל היה יכול לדקדק מסיפא, דקתני: "בי"ט כחמין שהוחמו בי"ט". אילימא רחיצת כל גופו — הא הוחמו מעי"ט שרי? והא לקמן אסר רחיצה בי"ט, דקאמר: "למחר נכנס ומזיע, אבל רוחץ — לא", ודוקא שטיפה שרי בבית החיצון! אלא, דרך הש"ס: מה שיכול לדקדק מרישא — מדקדק. ומיהו, קשה לרשב"א: דמגופה דמתניתין הוי מצי למידק, בלא הך ברייתא דמייתי, מדקתני: "ואסורים בשתיה" — כ"ש פניו, ידיו ורגליו דאסירי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:2:2.english: Rather, his face, his hands, and his feet, etc. - [The Gemara] could have deduced all of this from the concluding clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches: "[If] on a Festival, [it is] like hot water that was heated on a Festival." If you say [that this means] bathing one's entire body, [that would imply that] had they been heated on the eve of the Festival, it would be permitted [to bathe one's entire body on the Festival]! Yet later on (40a) [the baraita] prohibits bathing on a Festival, as it states: "The next day he enters and sweats, but he may not bathe," and specifically [only] rinsing is permitted in the outer room! Rather, it is the way of the Talmud that whatever it can deduce from the first clause [of a Mishnah], it deduces [from it]. However, the Rashba raises a difficulty: For from the Mishnah itself [the Gemara] could have deduced [this], without this baraita that it cites, from [the fact] that it teaches: "and they are forbidden for drinking" — all the more so [is washing] his face, his hands, and his feet forbidden!

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:3:1.hebrew: אלא אם כן ראויין לשתיה - נראה לר"י דווקא שמחמם אותם לצורך שתיה, אבל לצורך רחיצה, אע"ג דראויין לשתיה — אסרי ב"ש, דהא לית להו "מתוך" (ביצה ד' יב. ושם); ובפ"ב דביצה (ד' כא: ושם) אסרי ב"ש מדורה להתחמם כנגדה, ואע"ג דראויה היא לבשל ולאפות. ועוד אומר ר"י, דמהכא נמי יש לדקדק: דאי שרו ב"ש לצורך רחיצה משום דראויין לשתיה, א"כ לא אתיא מתני' אפי' כב"ש — דקתני: "ואסורין ברחיצה ומותרין בשתיה", ומדקתני "ומותרין בשתיה", מכלל דראויין לשתיה, ואפ"ה קתני דאסורין ברחיצה! אלא ודאי לא שרו ב"ש אלא כשעושה לצורך שתיה. ונראה לר"י דיכול לחמם אפי' ביותר מכדי שתיה, כדאמר בפרק הדר (עירובין ד' סח.): "נשייליה לאימיה, אי צריכה — נחיימו אגב אימיה"; ודוקא בכדי שיעור לרגליו, אבל לצורך כל גופו — לא. והיינו טעמא שהבלנים חשודים, דפעמים שיחממו עיקרן לרחיצה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:3:1.english: "Unless it is fit for drinking" - It appears to the Ri that [Beit Shammai permit this] specifically when one heats them for the purpose of drinking; but for the purpose of washing, even though they are fit for drinking, Beit Shammai forbid. For they do not accept [the principle of] mitokh (Beitzah 12a and there); and in the second chapter of Beitzah (21b and there), Beit Shammai forbid [making] a fire to warm oneself before it, even though it is fit for cooking and baking. And furthermore, the Ri says that from here too one can deduce [this]: For if Beit Shammai permitted [heating] for the purpose of washing because they are fit for drinking, if so, the Mishnah would not even be in accordance with Beit Shammai! For it teaches: "And they are forbidden for washing and permitted for drinking." And since it teaches "and permitted for drinking," by implication they are fit for drinking, and even so it teaches that they are forbidden for washing! Rather, Beit Shammai certainly permitted [it] only when one does [the heating] for the purpose of drinking. And it appears to the Ri that one may heat even more than the amount needed for drinking, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (Eruvin 68a): "Let us ask his mother; if she needs [hot water], let us heat [more] along with his mother['s need]." And [this applies] specifically to an amount sufficient for his feet, but for the needs of his entire body, no. And this is the reason that bathhouse attendants are suspected, for at times they would heat primarily for washing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:3:2.hebrew: וב"ה מתירין - משמע: דוקא לרגליו, אבל לצורך כל גופו — לא. וכן משמע בכולה שמעתין: דמחמירין בחמין שהוחמו בי"ט כחמין שהוחמו בשבת, וגזרו על הזיעה ביו"ט כמו בשבת, כדאמר בביצה בהמביא ולקמן (שבת דף מ. ושם). א"כ משמע שאסור לעשות הבערה משום רחיצה, שאם לא כן — לא היו גוזרים על הזיעה. ותימה: דמ"ש הבערה דרחיצה מהבערה דזיעה, דשרי מדאורייתא, כדמוכח התם? ואומר ר"י בשם ריב"א: דרחיצה אינה אלא לתענוג, ואסורה כמו מוגמר, דאסור בפ"ק דכתובות (ד' ז. וסם) משום דאין שוה לכל נפש; וכן משמע בירושלמי דהיינו טעמא דרחיצה. אבל זיעה שוה היא לכל נפש, דאינה תענוג אלא לבריאות. והא דתניא לקמן (שבת ד' מ.): "מרחץ שפקקו נקביו מעי"ט, למחר נכנס ומזיע" — ה"ה אפי' הוחם בו ביום, אלא נקט מעי"ט דאפ"ה דוקא מזיע, אבל רוחץ — לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:3:2.english: "And Beit Hillel permit" - This implies [that it is permitted] specifically for his feet, but for the needs of his entire body, [it is] not [permitted]. And so it is also implied throughout our entire sugya, that we are stringent regarding hot water that was heated on Yom Tov just like hot water that was heated on Shabbat; and they decreed against sweating [in a bathhouse] on Yom Tov just as on Shabbat, as [the Gemara] says in Beitza in [the chapter entitled] HaMevi (32b) and below (Shabbat 40a and there). If so, it implies that it is forbidden to kindle [a fire on Yom Tov] for the purpose of bathing, for if that were not so, they would not have decreed against sweating. And this is puzzling: For what is the difference between kindling for bathing and kindling for sweating, which is permitted by Torah law, as is proven there? And the Ri says in the name of the Riba that bathing is only for pleasure, and is forbidden like incense [mogmar], which is forbidden in the first chapter of Ketubot (7a and there) because it is not [a practice that is] equal for all people; and so it is implied in the Yerushalmi, that this is the reason regarding bathing. However, sweating is equal for all people, as it is not for pleasure, but for health. And as for that which is taught [in a baraita] below (Shabbat 40a): "A bathhouse whose vents were stopped up on the eve of Yom Tov, on the morrow one may enter and sweat" — the same law applies even if it was heated on that very day, but it taught [the case of] "from the eve of Yom Tov" [to teach] that even so, specifically sweating [is permitted], but bathing, no.

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:4:1.hebrew: בין בחמין בין בצונן - נראה לר"י, דהיינו אפי' חמין שהוחמו מע"ש — דהא אוסר אפי' צונן, ומסתמא בהנך חמין אסיר ר' יהודה. ועוד, דמסתמא לא מיירי בדעבדי איסורא. והאי תנא הוא דקאמר — היינו ר"ש. ועוד אומר ר"י, דיש להוכיח דבחמין שהוחמו מע"ש פליגי — דאמר בפרק חבית (לקמן שבת ד' קמז. ושם): "מה חמי טבריא חמין, אף מי מערה חמין; הרוחץ — דיעבד אין, לכתחילה לא; מכלל דלהשתטף — אפי' לכתחילה. מני? ר"ש היא, דתניא: לא ישתטף כו'". ואי בשהוחמו בשבת פליגי, אבל מערב שבת שרי ר' יהודה — אמאי צריך לאוקמה כר"ש? לוקמה כר' יהודה ובהוחמו מע"ש, דהא דומיא דחמי טבריא קתני:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:4:1.english: "Whether with hot water or with cold water" - It appears to the Ri that this means even hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve, for [Rabbi Meir] prohibits even cold water, and presumably Rabbi Yehuda prohibits with those [same] hot waters. And furthermore, presumably [the baraita] is not dealing with [a case where] they committed a transgression. And that which [the Gemara] said, "and it is [the opinion of] this tanna," refers to Rabbi Shimon. And furthermore, the Ri says that there is proof that they dispute regarding hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve: For it says in the chapter [entitled] Chavit (below, Shabbat 147a, and there): "Just as the hot springs of Tiberias are hot, so too the water of a cave is hot. One who bathes — after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. By inference, to rinse is [permitted] even ab initio. Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Shimon's, as it is taught: One may not rinse, etc." And if they dispute [only] regarding [water] that was heated on Shabbat, but [regarding water heated] from Shabbat eve Rabbi Yehuda permits, why did [the Gemara] need to establish it according to Rabbi Shimon? Let it establish it according to Rabbi Yehuda, and regarding [water] heated on Shabbat eve, for it teaches [cave water] similar to the hot springs of Tiberias!

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:5:1.hebrew: והא מעשה דאנשי טבריא בקרקע הוה ואסרי להו - הקשה ה"ר אליעזר ממי"ץ: מאי פריך? התם הוחמו בשבת, כדקתני: "כחמין שהוחמו בשבת", משמע דבהוחמו מע"ש שרי, והכא בהוחמו מע"ש פליגי, כדפרישית. ומפרש הר"ר יוסף: דס"ל להש"ס מדמחמיר ר"מ כ"כ דאוסר אפי' צונן, מחמיר נמי לאסור ע"ש אטו שבת. ולהכי פריך: "והא מעשה דאנשי טבריא בקרקע הוה ואסרי להו" בהוחמו בשבת, ורב חסדא קאמר: "אבל בקרקע ד"ה מותר" אפי' בהוחמו בשבת — דהא לר"מ, אי הוה אוסר להו בהוחמו בשבת, בהוחמו מע"ש נמי הוה אוסר. וקשה: דר"מ אוסר להשתטף בצונן אפי' בקרקע, כדמסיק דבקרקע פליגי; ובפרק שמונה שרצים (לקמן שבת דף קט. ושם) משמע דשרי, דקאמר התם: "רוחצין במי גרר ובמי חמתן ובמי עסיא ובמי טבריא, אבל לא בים הגדול", ורמינהו: "רוחצין במי טבריא ובים הגדול כו'", ומוקים בתרייתא כר' מאיר! וי"ל: דבקרקע דהכא דאסר — היינו דומיא דכלי, דדמי לרוחץ בחמין; והתם בנהר התירו, שנראה כמיקר בנהר, ואפי' בחמי טבריא לא דמי לאדם רוחץ בחמין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:5:1.english: "Wasn't the incident involving the people of Tiberias in the ground, and [the Rabbis] prohibited it to them?" - Rabbeinu Eliezer of Metz challenged: What is [the Gemara's] difficulty? There, [the water] was heated on Shabbat, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "like hot water that was heated on Shabbat," which implies that if it was heated on the eve of Shabbat, it is permitted; whereas here, they disagree with regard to [water] heated on the eve of Shabbat, as I explained. And Rabbeinu Yosef explains: The Talmud maintains that since Rabbi Meir is so stringent that he even prohibits cold [water], he is also stringent to prohibit [water heated on] the eve of Shabbat due to [water heated on] Shabbat. And for this reason [the Gemara] challenges: "Wasn't the incident involving the people of Tiberias in the ground, and they prohibited it to them" when heated on Shabbat; yet Rav Chisda said, "However, in the ground, everyone agrees that it is permitted," [which would imply] even when heated on Shabbat — for according to Rabbi Meir, if they prohibited it to them when heated on Shabbat, he would also prohibit [water] heated on the eve of Shabbat [as a decree due to Shabbat]. And [Tosafot] raises a difficulty: Rabbi Meir prohibits rinsing oneself in cold water even in the ground, as [the Gemara] concludes that they disagree [even] in the ground; yet in the chapter [entitled] Shemoneh Sheratzim (below, Shabbat 109a and there), it implies that it is permitted, as it says there: "One may bathe in the waters of Gerar, and in the waters of Chametan, and in the waters of Asya, and in the waters of Tiberias, but not in the Mediterranean Sea," and [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: "One may bathe in the waters of Tiberias and in the Mediterranean Sea, etc.," and establishes the latter [baraita] according to Rabbi Meir! And it can be answered: The [bathing in water in the] ground here that [Rabbi Meir] prohibits is similar to [bathing in] a vessel, as it resembles bathing in hot water; whereas there, they permitted [it] in a river, because it appears like cooling oneself off in a river, and even in the hot springs of Tiberias, it does not resemble a person bathing in hot water.

Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:6:1.hebrew: אמר רבה בר בר חנה הלכה כר' יהודה - אע"ג דר' יוחנן אית ליה הלכה כסתם משנה, הכא, משום דר' יהודה מכריע הוא, אין הלכה כסתם. וקשה, דבפרק קמא דפסחים (דף יג. ודף כא. ושם) פריך: "ונימא מר הלכה כר' מאיר, דסתם לן תנא כוותיה?", אע"ג דסבר דרבן גמליאל מכריע הוא, דפריך בתר הכי: "ונימא מר הלכה כרבן גמליאל, דהוה ליה מכריע?". וי"ל, דסתם דהכא גריע מההוא סתם: דהכא סתם במתני' ומחלוקת בברייתא, והלכה כמכריע; ומיהו, אי לאו הכרעה, הוה הלכה כסתם מתני', אע"ג דמחלוקת בברייתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 39b:6:1.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Even though Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that the halakha is in accordance with an unattributed Mishnah, here, because Rabbi Yehuda is a compromiser, the halakha is not in accordance with the unattributed [Mishnah]. And this is difficult, as in the first chapter of Pesachim (13a and 21a, and there) [the Gemara] challenges: "And let the Master say [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir, as the Tanna taught an unattributed [Mishnah] in accordance with him?", even though it maintained that Rabban Gamliel is a compromiser, as it challenges after that: "And let the Master say [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, as he is a compromiser?" And one can say that the unattributed [statement] here is inferior to that unattributed [statement]: for here, the unattributed [statement] is in the Mishnah while the dispute is in a baraita, and the halakha is in accordance with the compromiser. However, were it not for the compromise, the halakha would have been in accordance with the unattributed Mishnah, even though the dispute is in a baraita.
